messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P0 — Smart-routing policy errors on /v1/generate. Alert PD-1795002468. Symptoms: elevated 5xx from routing layer, repeated region fallbacks and sticky-variant reassignment causing user requests to oscillate between variants. Runbook: @on-call please acknowledge and triage.

jamie: ack, grabbing. I’m oncall for infra today. Can someone post a quick impact summary? Which customers/routes?

rachel: looks like it started ~22:18 UTC. Top affected routes: /v1/generate (production), /v1/chat (partial). Early telemetry shows spike in token-latency and ~3.8% error rate for traffic hitting policy mp-staged-42. Jobs: tracing shows fallback loops between us-east-1 <-> us-west-2.

aditya: I’m seeing policy mp-staged-42 has a bad variant mapping — it references variant `redwood-v2-opt` for canary but that model binary lacks the expected signature for streaming endpoints, so router rejects and falls back. The sticky routing code then reassigns the session to the canary again on retries, causing loop.

mika: confirmed in logs. sample:``` 
2026-03-14T22:18:12Z router[proxy]: decision mp-staged-42 -> try variant=redwood-v2-opt (id=var_874)
2026-03-14T22:18:12Z model-proxy[var_874]: ERR incompatible-api: streaming not supported
2026-03-14T22:18:12Z router[proxy]: fallback -> variant=redwood-v1-stable (id=var_102)
2026-03-14T22:18:13Z router[proxy]: sticky assign session= sess_0xabc -> mp-staged-42
2026-03-14T22:18:14Z router[proxy]: detect oscillation count=5 for session sess_0xabc
trace_id=trc_1795_0001
``` 

jamie: that matches the symptom (oscillation detection). Immediate mitigation options: 1) disable the canary/staged policy mp-staged-42; 2) remove sticky assignment for sessions affected; 3) pin traffic to stable variant. We should pick minimally invasive to stop customer impact quickly.

rachel: I can disable the policy from console (Control Plane -> Routing -> mp-staged-42). I’ll also create a temp rule to prefer stable variant for existing sticky sessions.

aditya: if you disable the policy we need to ensure no race causing orphan sticky states — also purge prefix/KV cache for routing decisions to avoid reusing old sticky assignments.

mika: I can run the purge and restart route-proxy on the two edge clusters that saw the highest error rates.

jamie: go for disable+purge+pin. Call it out when done so we can watch metrics.

rachel: disabling mp-staged-42 now. ``disabled_by=0403-rachel``

infra-bot: Deploy action: policy mp-staged-42 state set to DISABLED by rachel (ui). Change propagated to control-plane nodes in 12s. Rollout id: roll_1795002473.

mika: purging sticky assignments and kv-cache on routers in us-east-1 and us-west-2.

mika: purge commands run:``` 
# run from ops box
./routectl purge-sticky --policy mp-staged-42 --clusters us-east-1,us-west-2
./routectl purge-kv --key-prefix sticky(mp-staged-42)
``` 

samir: restarted route-proxy on edge-1 and edge-2. Restart logs show no errors. trace ids: trc_1795_0002, trc_1795_0003.

jamie: monitoring dashboards. latency/error graph starting to flatten. Customer-visible errors dropping from 3.8% -> 0.6% over last 6m. Good so far.

aditya: we should still investigate root cause: why variant mapping was incompatible. Possibly a model onboarding step omitted the streaming capability flag or the compatibility check failed.

rachel: I found an onboarding PR that changed variant id mapping for mp-staged-42 without updating compatibility metadata — PR #4823. Looks like review didn’t catch the missing capability tag.

jamie: ok for immediate followup: 1) Rollback PR mappings for mp-staged-42 (aditya), 2) Add automated compatibility check in policy deployer to validate streaming/struct output API surface (mika + eng-ml), 3) Postmortem writeup + remediation CL (rachel). Who owns the postmortem?

aditya: I’ll revert the mapping and add a guard in the deployer. I’ll open a PR and link it.

mika: Eng-ML, we should add a lightweight model capability manifest check that fails canary if required features missing. I’ll sponsor the eval.

jamie: handover — I’ll leave this as acknowledged and move to follow-up state. On-call handoff: jamie -> rachel for next 2 hours. If anything pops, page me.

rachel: will own follow-up and postmortem. Drafting postmortem doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1795 (placeholder link). Will include impact numbers and timeline.

infra-bot: Incident status changed: Mitigated by policy disable + cache purge. Severity downgraded to P1 at 22:32 UTC.

jamie: proposed action items in summary (copying to thread):
- Immediate: disabled mp-staged-42, purged sticky assignments, pinned to stable variant; route-proxy restarts. (done)
- Short-term: revert variant mapping PR #4823, add deploy-time compatibility checks, add automatic canary health failover after X errors to disable canary automatically. (owners: aditya, mika)
- Postmortem: rachel to draft, include metrics and timeline, schedule blameless review. (owner: rachel)

mika: small ops note — add a metric in routing indicating "sticky-oscillation-count" to trigger alerts before customer errors spike. I'll file a ticket.

rachel: confirmed customer impact: ~6 internal teams briefly saw elevated error rates, estimated customer requests impacted ~0.5% of total for 14 minutes. No data exfiltration. CS notified.

samir: thumbs on runbook updates. Will add exact commands we ran into ops-runbook repo.

jamie: thanks everyone. If nothing else, I'll close the immediate incident thread once postmortem created. :thumbsup:
